title: CVE-2026-6253: proxy credentials leak over redirect-to proxy
excerpt:
## Summary:

  When libcurl follows a redirect and the new URL causes proxy re-selection, proxy credentials learned from the originally selected proxy URL can remain in per-transfer state and be reused for the next proxy. In the validated case, a redirect from http:// to https:// switches selection from http_proxy to https_proxy, but credentials from http_proxy=http://user:pass@... are still sent to the https_proxy even when the https_proxy URL contains no credentials. A redirecting server can therefore cause libcurl to send Proxy-Authorization intended for proxy A to proxy B on proxy B’s first request. This appears limited to proxy credentials carried in transfer state, not the intentionally global CURLOPT_PROXYUSERNAME / CURLOPT_PROXYPASSWORD case. As a control, requesting the HTTPS URL directly with the same https_proxy does not send Proxy-Authorization to proxy B. I reproduced this on a local build and observed proxy B receive Proxy-Authorization: Basic dXNlcjpwYXNz on the initial CONNECT.

  ## Affected version

  Reproduced with:
  curl 8.20.0-DEV (Linux) libcurl/8.20.0-DEV OpenSSL/3.0.2 zlib/1.2.11 brotli/1.0.9 zstd/1.4.8 libidn2/2.3.2 libpsl/0.21.0 nghttp2/1.43.0 OpenLDAP/2.5.20

  Protocols: dict file ftp ftps gopher gophers http https imap imaps ipfs ipns ldap ldaps mqtt mqtts pop3 pop3s rtsp smtp smtps telnet tftp ws wss

  Features: alt-svc AsynchDNS brotli HSTS HTTP2 HTTPS-proxy IDN IPv6 Largefile libz PSL SSL threadsafe TLS-SRP UnixSockets zstd

  Git commit used: 935e1f9963a12ac1a880df538b23b824d2fea7bb

  Platform:
  Linux 6.8.0-1044-azure #50~22.04.1-Ubuntu SMP Wed Dec  3 15:13:22 UTC 2025 x86_64 GNU/Linux

  ## Steps To Reproduce:

  1. Start an HTTP origin on 127.0.0.1:8000 that returns a redirect from /redir to https://127.0.0.1:8443/final.
  2. Start an HTTPS origin on 127.0.0.1:8443 that serves /final. Any certificate is sufficient; curl -k is enough for local reproduction.
  3. Start two HTTP-family proxies and log incoming request headers:
      - Proxy A on 127.0.0.1:8081
      - Proxy B on 127.0.0.1:8082
  4. Run:

  http_proxy=http://user:pass@127.0.0.1:8081 \
  https_proxy=http://127.0.0.1:8082 \
  /path/to/curl -k -L http://127.0.0.1:8000/redir

  5. Observe that the first HTTP request goes through proxy A and includes credentials for proxy A.
  6. After the redirect to https://127.0.0.1:8443/final, libcurl re-selects proxy B via
explain: The evidence does not settle it either way.
summary: A redirecting server can cause libcurl to disclose credentials intended for one proxy to a different proxy under separate administrative control.

claims.text: Proxy credentials learned from the originally selected proxy URL can remain in per-transfer state and be reused for the next proxy after a redirect changes proxy selection.
claims.reasoning: The provided source code only shows the definition of CURLPROXY_HTTPS (include/curl/curl.h:794). The implementation code for proxy selection, credential extraction from proxy URLs, per-transfer state management during redirects, and Proxy-Authorization header generation is not included in the provided source. Without the relevant functions (likely in lib/http_proxy.c, lib/url.c, or lib/transfer.c), the claim cannot be verified or contradicted.

claims.text: The issue occurs when a redirect switches from an http:// URL to an https:// URL, causing libcurl to reuse credentials from the http_proxy to the https_proxy.
claims.reasoning: Same as C1: the code that handles proxy selection based on URL scheme (http vs https) and credential reuse across proxy changes during redirects is not provided. The symbols CURLOPT_PROXY and CURLOPT_HTTPS_PROXY are mentioned but their handling code is absent.

claims.text: A redirect from http:// to https:// that changes the proxy selection from http_proxy to https_proxy triggers the reuse of credentials.
claims.reasoning: The redirect handling logic that triggers proxy re-selection and the code path that fails to clear proxy credentials when the proxy changes are not in the provided source.

claims.text: Proxy-B receives Proxy-Authorization: Basic dXNlcjpwYXNz on its first request, even though its URL contains no credentials.
claims.reasoning: The CONNECT request generation and Proxy-Authorization header construction code is not provided. The claim describes observed behavior that would be decided by proxy connection setup code not shown.

claims.text: Run curl with http_proxy=http://user:pass@127.0.0.1:8081 and https_proxy=http://127.0.0.1:8082, then follow a redirect from http://127.0.0.1:8000/redir to https://127.0.0.1:8443/final; proxy B will receive Proxy-Authorization.
claims.reasoning: The reproduction steps describe a concrete scenario, but the code implementing the described flow (proxy env var parsing, redirect following, proxy re-selection, credential carry-over) is not in the provided source.

claims.text: The disclosure crosses a real proxy trust boundary and can expose reusable proxy secrets before any authentication challenge from the second proxy.
claims.reasoning: This is an impact assessment dependent on C1-C4 being true. Since the underlying mechanism cannot be verified from the provided code, the impact claim also cannot be verified.

key_reasons: The report describes a specific, plausible credential leak across proxy trust boundaries during redirect-induced proxy re-selection.

The provided curl source code excerpt contains only the CURLPROXY_HTTPS constant definition (include/curl/curl.h:794). None of the implementation code for proxy URL parsing, credential extraction, redirect handling, per-transfer state management, or Proxy-Authorization header generation is included.

Deterministic checks only confirm CURLOPT_PROXYUSERNAME and CURLOPT_PROXYPASSWORD exist, but the report explicitly states the issue is about credentials embedded in the proxy URL (http://user:pass@proxy), not those global options.

A human reviewer needs to examine the proxy handling and redirect code (likely in lib/http_proxy.c, lib/url.c, lib/transfer.c) to determine if proxy credentials from the original proxy URL are incorrectly retained in per-transfer state when the proxy changes due to a scheme change (http→https).
